subject.id: globgrph stitch producer, archive carry-forward -- CARRIER: NODES
subject.declared_domain: The NODE half of one mechanism: derive_stitch.load_aws_layer() reads the nightly AWS snapshot, and derive_runner.archive_snapshot() writes that snapshot AFTER folding this producer's own output into it, so every node this producer emitted last cycle arrives back as INPUT. Covers the nodes carrying source=portal-stitch in the snapshot -- their re-typing, their duplicate copies, and their retirement. Does NOT cover props on those nodes (the props carrier card) or edges between them (the edges carrier card): the same question was answered separately, and differently, on each.

NOT RE-READ BY THIS CARD: the round-7 egress hold forbids any act whose effect reaches AWS, so every snapshot number here is read from the record of that read and carries its basis accordingly.

methodology.how: derive_stitch builds the portal/pipeline subgraph, unions it with the AWS layer loaded from s3://opal-313476888478-globgrph via snapshots/latest.txt, merges stitch members onto canonical ids, and emits one artifact. The nodes arriving in that AWS layer with source=portal-stitch are not third-party data: they are this producer's own emission from the previous cycle, folded in by derive_runner.ingest_stitch_artifact and archived by derive_runner.archive_snapshot. Two producer-side handlers exist for them, and they answer different failures. _retype_prior_cycle re-types a prior cycle's provisional names by the producer's own source stamp, so a vocabulary change converges in ONE cycle instead of two. _collapse_stitch_copies then keeps one node per id, preferring the object this run emitted -- identified by Python object identity (fresh_objs), taken before the union, because after the union a fresh node and its archived copy are indistinguishable by their data.

cadence.declared_rhythm: Two clocks, 23 hours apart, and the gap between them IS the carry-forward. The producer (CodeBuild opal-stitch-produce) runs on cron(0 3 * * ? *); the derive that folds its artifact in and archives the snapshot runs on cron(0 2 * * ? *). So an emission made at 03:00Z is folded and archived at the NEXT 02:00Z and read back by the producer at the 03:00Z after that.
cadence.actual_trigger: EventBridge schedule rules, one per side. No success-of-upstream trigger: both sides fire on their own clock, which is why a producer-side removal is not synchronised with the archive that still holds it.
cadence.live_instance_age: The 03:00Z rule-initiated nightly of 2026-09-10 succeeded and its artifact is what the round-6 grain baseline was signed on; this card did not re-read the live rule.

key.evidence: infra/aws/globgrph/derive_stitch.py:224-231 @f3b5f26f77 -- the unification rewrites node ids AND edge endpoints through one map, and the map is a local variable, not an artifact. Nothing persists the pre-merge id, so a consumer holding yesterday's id cannot resolve it except by re-running the same merge. That is what makes the key unstable rather than merely derived, and why the freshness test at :126 had to fall back to Python object identity: two nodes legitimately share an id across the union.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: A COMPLETE-LOOKING GRAPH WITH LAST CYCLE'S NODES IN IT, exit 0, no warning, no count. The union succeeds, the per-class dedup collapses identical copies, every class-level check passes, and the grain sentinel reads counts that are correct for a population nobody meant to keep. The one loud failure in this carrier is the opposite case: when the re-type was ABSENT the four provisional names survived at their carried counts and the grain sentinel REFUSED to publish -- the producer's only mechanical tell, and it fires on a type change, not on a stale carry.
silent_degrade_paths: RETIREMENT IS THE OPEN ONE, AND IT IS THE ROUND'S LESSON ON THIS CARRIER: _collapse_stitch_copies drops an archived copy only when the same id is in this run's fresh emission (derive_stitch.py:437-455 @f3b5f26f77). A node the producer STOPS emitting is not in fresh_ids, so nothing drops it and it is served for another cycle -- the nodes-carrier form of silently idempotent under a fixed emission, silently wrong under a shrinking one. There is no node-side equivalent of the edges carrier's drop-on-read.

A node re-typed by _retype_prior_cycle carries retyped_from, which the collapse USED to read as its freshness signal; the moment the snapshot itself held canonical names nothing was re-typed, the signal went empty, and the tie-break fell to dict iteration order (measured: NFRA_CLDGRPH-W2-S69). The fresh_objs remedy closes this path; the row is kept here because the failure was a SIGNAL going quiet, not a signal going wrong, and the next inferred freshness mark will fail the same way.
A node whose provisional type is absent from PROVISIONAL_TO_CANONICAL is carried unchanged with no count -- PORTAL_BUNDLE is the live instance.

verdict.why: Every row is measured and two of the three failures this carrier can produce are closed at the producer: re-typing converges a vocabulary change in one cycle, and the duplicate copy is resolved by an object identity no data field can drift out from under. The third is OPEN and named: a node the producer stops emitting is never dropped on read, so a SHRINKING node population is carried forward silently, with no error and no count. Usable for anything that only ever adds or re-types members; NOT usable, without the named remedy, as evidence that a node the producer no longer emits is gone.
blocking_defects: NO DROP-ON-READ FOR STITCH NODES (owner 0.8.0_AE_CloudComp): derive_stitch.py:437-455 @f3b5f26f77 drops an archived copy only when this run re-emitted the same id. The edges carrier solved exactly this at :141-142 by dropping its own prior-cycle edge type on read and COUNTING what it dropped; the node side has no counterpart. Remedy shape, from the carrier that already did it: drop this producer's own prior-cycle nodes on read and emit the count, so a shrink shows up as a number instead of as nothing.
